recipes.name: Sardines with Sun-Dried Tomato and Capers
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.75 ounce) can sardines packed in olive oil, drained (such as King Oscar®)
1 pinch salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 pinch crushed red pepper flakes, or to taste

steps.text: Place the sardines on a small plate. Squeeze the lemon half over the sardines; season with salt, black pepper, cayenne pepper, oregano, thyme, and crushed red pepper flakes. Scatter the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, and capers over the mixture.

raw_recipe.headline: Sardines with Sun-Dried Tomato and Capers
raw_recipe.description: The mixture of ingredients in this recipe really balances the fish flavor, and turns a can of sardines into a tasty meal. Pair with quinoa and a side of sauteed spinach.
raw_recipe.name: Sardines with Sun-Dried Tomato and Capers

1 pinch salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 pinch crushed red pepper flakes, or to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Place the sardines on a small plate. Squeeze the lemon half over the sardines; season with salt, black pepper, cayenne pepper, oregano, thyme, and crushed red pepper flakes. Scatter the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, and capers over the mixture.

review.reviewBody: FYI, this recipe will taste great without the sun-dried tomatoes and capers. And you can omit or decrease the amount of cayenne pepper. The key is seasoning with the herbs, garlic and lemon. Hope you enjoy!

I love this recipe. I am a salty, briny seafood person - but even if you aren't, this recipe is so flavorful the fish is not at all overpowering. I like to add half a dozen chopped kalamata olives, serve on a bed of baby spinach or arugala, and drizzle with a tiny bit of olive oil. I eat this often year-round, but it's my favorite quick dinner to make in the summer when it's too hot to turn on my oven or use my stovetop! YUM!

I made an allrecipes account just so I can give this 5 stars. Canned sardines never tasted so good! If it's cold out I suggest putting the tin can directly under the broiler for 5 minutes along with the chopped garlic then assembling on your plate as directed. Warmed me right up. Thanks for the recipe. I will be making this again for sure.

Simple, but tastes “fancy”. I used jarred sun-dried tomatoes packed in olive oil and salt-packed capers, which I rinsed and dried. Served over a simple salad if mild iceberg with a splash of olive oil and balsamic

This is a quick and easy low carb snack or meal. It's so simple and convenient. The seasonings and lemon complement the sardines very nicely, although I would probably go light on the thyme next time. A little definitely goes a long way with thyme! I added a whole lemon (and wouldn't hesitate to add more) and more crushed red pepper and cayenne because I like a little more spice. I also added paprika and omitted the capers and salt, instead adding about 1/4 cup of pesto.

Great way to make sardines into a nice meal for one. I used Costco's Organic No Salt Seasoning in place of garlic, and Cholula Chili Garlic Hot Sauce in place of cayenne. Don't even think of trying this without the lemon; it's essential.

Wow! This was delicious. Loads of bold flavors. For someone new to sardines, the ingredients masked any fishiness and enhanced the flavor. I had it over a slice of toasted gluten-free bread. Perfect! Will definitely make again. Side note: I did not drain the sardines but instead used the olive oil it was packed in.

OMG!
This is my new favorite way to eat sardines!
I love the difference flavor combination and the heat!
It's great on toasted sourdough bread with a fried egg!
I am now a sardines junkie!

Thank you, previous review writers! I approached this recipe aware of the benefits of eating oily fish, yet not a fan. So many positive reviews encouraged me to give it a try, and I'm so glad I did! Delicious! I made one or two adaptions. I had no sundried tomatoes, so didn't include them, and I used lime instead of lemon. Served on a bed of watercress with a wholemeal roll. A very tasty lunch filled with goodness!
I used Wild Caught Sardines in oil and lemon; no fishy odor. Did not add the salt and reduced the "heat" and lemon . Best sardines I have eate.

This is a great fast way to get more sardines into your diet (they are packed with goodness and cost so much less than the salmon everyone seems bent on getting us to eat). I made this and served over mixed green with a dressing made from the olive oil the sardines were packed in and lemon juice. I also added a few pitted and coarsely chopped kalamata olives I had on hand. It was delicious! But of course, I bet it would be a five star amazing recipe with fresh Sardines.
Love the tang of the various spices with the sardines. I serve it for myself over a bed of Spring Mix. It works perfectly with my Mediterranean diet.
I used garlic powder instead of fresh...lazy. This was incredible!
Delicious snack! I was going to have it solo but ripped off a piece of a rustic loaf of bread and this was absolutely amazing for something so simple. Definitely filling my pantry with Sardines now!
No changes to this recipe. I enjoyed over some Romaine lettuce.
As another reviewer put it....you will like sardines after eating this recipe. Will make again. Made this exactly as written.

Oh, my god! So simple to prepare, and so delicious! I followed the recipe to the letter. I must say it is not enough for one serving. Maybe because I had just a salad as a side dish. But for a light meal,it does well. Next time (because it sure will be in my menu very frequently) I'll have it with boiled potatoes or rice in a sort of warm salad. If you are put off by the fishy taste or smell, let me tell you that this meal softens it a lot. One last thing, I looked at the photo in this recipe and I realized that I didn't add enough olive oil as you'll see in my photo.
This recipe was absolutely delicious!! I love sardines but this recipe put them over the top!!!
